method: Direct verification against Anthropic's own Tier-0 primary sources (Claude Code documentation page and changelog, both fetched live) plus Anthropic's own ClaudeDevs account announcement on X, cross-checked against independent Tier-2 coverage (9to5Mac). No fresh verifier/falsifier sub-agent pair was spun up this pass -- verification was done in-session directly against the primary source, given this cycle's ~29-minute time budget -- but every load-bearing claim traces to Anthropic's own documentation of its own product, which is the strongest possible source type for a first-party feature announcement. A separate search for security criticism or dispute of this specific shipped feature found only generic/pre-existing feature-request discussion and unrelated Claude Desktop coverage, nothing disputing what was announced.
origin_items: Surfaced from this cycle's fresh ingest (data/raw/2026-08-08/techmeme.json), a Techmeme item citing 9to5Mac's coverage of Anthropic's announcement.

claims.text: Anthropic released cross-session messaging in Claude Code version 2.1.224, dated 7 August 2026, letting one Claude Code session send a text message to another using a new SendMessage tool, with ListAgents used to discover reachable sessions
claims.reasoning: Confirmed directly from Anthropic's own Claude Code changelog (version 2.1.224, dated 2026-08-07) and the dedicated cross-session-messaging documentation page, both first-party Tier-0 sources describing Anthropic's own product.

claims.text: The feature is available on macOS and Linux (including Linux inside WSL 2); it is not available on native Windows, and is not available on Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry
claims.reasoning: Stated explicitly in the documentation's 'Availability' section.

claims.text: A message is plain text only, never the sender's conversation history or files; same-machine delivery uses a local per-session socket, cross-machine delivery goes through Anthropic's servers via Remote Control and is reply-only on the receiving side
claims.reasoning: Stated explicitly in the documentation's message-delivery and cross-machine-messaging sections.

claims.text: Delivery of an incoming message is controlled per-session by the crossSessionInbound setting and the sessions' permission modes, with held messages defaulting to a five-minute expiry (dialogExpiry) if not approved
claims.reasoning: Stated explicitly in the documentation's 'Control inbound messages' section.

claims.text: Anthropic's own ClaudeDevs account publicly announced the feature the same day, describing it as sending a summary rather than history or files
claims.reasoning: Direct quote from ClaudeDevs' own X post, matching the documentation's description.

falsifier_notes: Targeted search for 'Claude Code cross-session messaging security concern criticism' found only pre-existing GitHub feature-request threads (predating this shipped release) and generic Claude Code security best-practice writeups, plus an unrelated Claude Desktop browser-access story -- nothing disputing the accuracy of what Anthropic shipped or announced. dedup-check returned zero matches against the archive -- standalone story, not a duplicate or follow-up of any existing entry. This is a first-party product-feature story (Anthropic describing its own shipped product), which is a different evidentiary category from the business-deal/personnel-rumor stories held in watching -- the independence rule (verification.md policy/independence) applies to third-party claims about a company; a company's own accurate self-description of a shipped feature is itself the Tier-0 primary confirmation.
